Container.Name: PassForge
Container.Overview:
PassForge is a privacy-focused password analysis and secure passphrase generation tool.
Evaluate password strength using zxcvbn and entropy analysis, check passwords against the Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) breach database using the k-Anonymity range API, and generate cryptographically secure passphrases from the official EFF large and short wordlists.
Password analysis, SHA-1 hashing, breach-result matching, and passphrase generation run locally in your browser. For breach checks, only the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 hash are sent to the PassForge backend, which retrieves the matching HIBP range. Your plaintext password and complete hash never leave your browser.
PassForge also provides configurable passphrase length, wordlists, separators, entropy targets, batch generation, dark mode, and Progressive Web App support.
No additional services are required. Redis is optional and can be used for shared rate-limit storage; by default, PassForge uses built-in in-memory rate limiting.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: password passwords passphrase passphrases password strength entropy HIBP Have I Been Pwned security generator EFF zxcvbn
Container.Requires: No additional services are required. Internet access is required only for Have I Been Pwned breach checks. Password analysis and passphrase generation remain available independently of HIBP.
Container.Changes:
v1.2.1 - Hardened the default container runtime with a read-only root filesystem, restricted /tmp tmpfs, all Linux capabilities dropped, and no-new-privileges enabled. Changed the default Unraid WebUI host port to 5150.
v1.1.0 - Moved password analysis, HIBP suffix matching, and passphrase generation into the browser. The server now receives only the five-character HIBP hash prefix. Added verified browser dependencies and expanded privacy and security testing.
v1.0.1 - Added automated Bandit, pip-audit, and Trivy security gates; upgraded Alpine runtime packages.
v1.0.0 - Initial PassForge release.
